description: X5.7. A 1.35 kg, 450 mm X quadcopter (GroundSpatial - Free3D - RigidBody3D, Z up) flies a take-off, a square-ish mission with a 90 degree yaw turn and a landing in 18 s under a PX4-style cascade (position P 50 Hz -> velocity PID 50 Hz -> thrust vector -> attitude P 250 Hz -> body-rate PID 500 Hz -> mixer 500 Hz -> ESC speed loop 500 Hz -> ElectricDrive + Propeller on every rotor, 3S pack). The controller sees only the sensors: a 500 Hz IMU (bias + noise + Butterworth low-pass), a 50 Hz position/velocity/heading fix and the library/NavFilter.jl observer; the plant sits on four Hertz ContactPoint legs and flies in a 0.4 / -0.2 m/s wind with 0.5 m/s gusts. Every number below is a measurement of this model on the real worker (reltol 1e-4); design/design.py derives the gains and checks the loops. The quadcopter-repeat twin is the same document stopped at 9 s on the same grid: the deterministic discrete parts (hash noise, ticks) must reproduce the 18 s run bit for bit.

checks.note: the airframe starts at rest on its four legs, the CoM 0.085 m above the ground plane
disarmed on the ground: the four ContactPoint legs carry the whole weight m g = 1.35 * 9.81 N (measured 13.2546)
take-off to the 1 m hover (set-point: minimum-jerk climb from t = 1 s over 3 s): overshoot 0.2 %, within +-2 cm from 2.7 s after the start of the climb
hover altitude reached: 1.0859 m (set-point 1.085 m)
the hover is held inside a 2 cm band (measured 1.1 cm: wind gusts and the velocity integrator catching the 4 % mass error of the thrust feedforward)
hover rotor speed sqrt(m g / (4 kT)) = 482.4 rad/s (4607 rpm), measured 482.15
hover current of the pack: 99 W electrical for 13.3 N of thrust at 12.4 V
waypoint (2, 0): reached at the end of leg 1 (measured 2.0013)
waypoint (2, 2): reached at the end of leg 2 (measured 2.016)
the 90 degree yaw turn flown during leg 2 (measured 1.6026 rad)
waypoint tracking in x over the three legs: RMS 4.6 cm (limit 6 cm) against 2 m moves in 2.5 to 3 s
waypoint tracking in y: RMS 5.0 cm
altitude held while the airframe tilts and turns: RMS 0.84 cm
distance to the set-point never exceeds 15 cm during the mission (measured 12.0 cm)
attitude bounded: the tilt stays below 17 degrees (measured 0.247 rad = 14.2 degrees, the thrust-vector limit of the position controller is 25 degrees)
peak tilt of the acceleration phase of the legs
the quaternion kinematics keep |q| = 1 (measured 7e-13)
landed: back on the legs, CoM at 0.0847 m
after the landing the four legs carry m g again (measured 13.2435)
rotor speed below the 774.6 rad/s of the 8.5 N thrust limit of the mixer (measured peak 557.6 rad/s = 5325 rpm)
peak rotor speed of the mission (the rotors never get near the thrust limit)
the ESC command never exceeds the open-circuit voltage of the 3S pack (measured peak 8.4 V)
motor current peak at the spin-up from standstill (measured 44 A; the ESC current limit is 25 A of voltage headroom)
pack current peak 62 A at arming
the 18 s flight used 1.35 % of the 3 Ah pack
the navigation filter attitude error stays below 1.7 degrees (measured 1.08 degrees) with a 0.2 deg/s gyro bias and noise
the estimate is not the truth: the controller flies on a 0.5 degree RMS attitude error
position estimate error (measured 2.9 cm; the fix has 2 cm noise per sample)
velocity estimate error (measured 0.108 m/s; the fix has 0.05 m/s noise per sample)
the raw gyro is the truth plus a 0.004 rad/s bias and 0.003 rad/s noise: RMS 0.0069 rad/s
the rate loop follows its set-point (RMS 0.049 rad/s on a 0.9 rad/s peak rate)
no solver failure, no causal conflict, no frame mismatch, no derivative-causal store, no algebraic loop and no event-limit stop
same hover altitude as the 18 s run (the twin only stops earlier)

compare.note: determinism of the sampled sensors: the hash-noise sequence of the IMU is a pure function of the tick counter, so a second run reproduces it exactly
determinism of the discrete filter and controller chain (500 Hz navigation filter)
and the closed-loop plant trajectory (the continuous part reproduces to the integrator's determinism)
